scope: Primary literature screen for quantitative raw/cooked onion quercetin evidence potentially comparable to Stage C food record B011-HPLC-06.

target_record.analyte: Quercetin aglycone as a directly targeted HPLC-PDA analyte, with LC-ESI-QTOF/MS identity verification
target_record.method_note: The Stage C source chromatographically reports quercetin as its own analyte; it does not report acid-hydrolyzed total quercetin equivalents.

required_for_quantitative_comparison: same compound form and reported measurand (free analyte versus hydrolysis-released or equivalent totals must not be conflated)
same food species and edible matrix; cultivar or variety must be known or explicitly treated as a population-level range
same raw/cooked state and compatible cooking condition for the modeled endpoint
same unit and measurement basis; no inferred dry/fresh, cooked/raw, or yield conversion
traceable analytical calibration and quantitative data locator in primary article or recognized database
replication and uncertainty sufficiently described to interpret the reference
screen_policy.software_gate: stageC/src/stage_c/validation.py::compare_to_reference requires units and measurement basis to match and requires reference ID/source reference for the published_data_comparison layer. This literature screen additionally requires scientific analyte and condition commensurability; code-level unit/basis acceptance alone is not a scientific eligibility decision.
screen_policy.value_policy: No values were copied from abstracts, third-party reproductions, or unverified graphs. No numeric source fixture was made because no candidate clears the scientific comparison gate.

candidates.citation: Watanabe J, Muro T, Kobori M, Takano-Ishikawa Y. Changes in Quercetin Content and Antioxidant Capacity of Quercetin-Rich Onion Cultivar 'Quer-Gold' During Cooking. Nippon Shokuhin Kagaku Kogaku Kaishi. 2018;65(2):63-66.
candidates.source_access: Open primary publisher PDF; full text inspected.
candidates.quantitative_locator: Table 1, pp. 64-65: quercetin content during sautéing; Table 3/Figure 1, p. 65: cooked onion dishes. Table 1 heading and associated methods/results §§1(1)-1(4), 2(1).
candidates.food_and_matrix: Allium cepa edible bulb; 2014 Hokkaido-grown cultivars Quer-Gold and Kitamomiji 2000; bulbs held at 0°C before use.
candidates.analyte_and_form: Quercetin reported as quercetin aglycone equivalents after analytical hydrolysis of quercetin glycosides. It is a total hydrolyzable quercetin measure, not free aglycone concentration.
candidates.raw_cooked_conditions: Raw and sautéed onion. 4 mm dice, 6% canola/salad oil, 160°C; sampled at 20% and 50% mass loss. Cooked dishes used sautéed onion at a specified raw-onion-equivalent amount.
candidates.units_and_basis: Table 1 reports mg/100 g initial fresh onion weight, correcting for oil added and water lost during sautéing. Dish values are per serving.
candidates.yield_and_mass_balance: Mass-loss endpoints measured at 20% and 50%; recipe portions specify raw-onion-equivalent mass. Cooking yield is documented for the sauté treatment.
candidates.analytical_method: Prominence HPLC using the authors' previously validated onion aglycone method; hydrolysis converts quercetin glycosides to aglycone equivalents before quantification.
candidates.replication: Ten bulbs of each cultivar contributed edible material; cooking and recipe preparation performed three times; two sample/measurement replicates were averaged; Table 1 n=3, mean ± SD.
blockers: The measurand is total hydrolysis-released quercetin aglycone equivalents, while B011-HPLC-06 is direct quercetin aglycone; those values are not chemically interchangeable.
The controlled cultivars (Quer-Gold, Kitamomiji 2000; Hokkaido 2014) do not match the unspecified Melbourne-market cultivar in B011-HPLC-06.
No Stage C cooked onion prediction with a matching cultivar, sauté endpoint and total-equivalent measurand was present for this workstream to compare.

candidates.citation: Cattivelli A, Conte A, Martini S, Tagliazucchi D. Influence of Cooking Methods on Onion Phenolic Compounds Bioaccessibility. Foods. 2021;10(5):1023.
candidates.source_access: Open publisher and PMC full text; tables, cooking methods, and analysis section inspected.
candidates.quantitative_locator: Table 1 (cooking conditions and weight loss); Tables 2-3 (individual compounds in raw/cooked yellow- and red-skinned onion); Figure 1 (quercetin derivatives normalized to initial fresh weight); Methods §§2.2-2.7.
candidates.food_and_matrix: Allium cepa L. bulb, yellow-skinned and red-skinned retail onions from Reggio Emilia, Italy.
candidates.analyte_and_form: Individual free quercetin and multiple quercetin glycosides are listed; however, the methods state flavonols are quantified in quercetin-3-O-glucoside equivalents.
candidates.raw_cooked_conditions: Raw plus baked (180°C, 30 min), boiled (100°C, 30 min; onion:water 1:5, drained 30 s), fried (sunflower oil, 140°C, 8 min), and grilled (110°C, 15 min). Onion peeled and sliced to about 0.3 cm.
candidates.units_and_basis: Tables 2-3: mg compound/100 g raw or cooked onion. Figure 1: mg/100 g original fresh weight. These are distinct denominators and cannot be silently mixed.
candidates.yield_and_mass_balance: Initial/final mass and weight-loss ratios recorded by cooking method in Table 1.
candidates.analytical_method: HPLC coupled to electrospray ion-trap mass spectrometry; water/methanol/formic-acid extraction. Flavonols quantified as quercetin-3-O-glucoside equivalents.
candidates.replication: Each cooking experiment in three trials; each analysis in triplicate; mean ± SD. Retail source cultivar, lot size, and biological lot replication are not resolved in the inspected methods.
blockers: Although quercetin is individually listed, the stated flavonol calibration is quercetin-3-O-glucoside equivalents; the published mass concentration is not traceably equivalent to B011's authentic-quercetin-standard result.
B011 has no cultivar identity, while this source separates yellow- and red-skinned retail onions.
The article provides cooked measurements but no matched Stage C cooked prediction was available in this isolated workstream.

candidates.citation: Nishimuro H, et al. Estimated Daily Intake and Seasonal Food Sources of Quercetin in Japan. Nutrients. 2015;7(4):2345-2358.
candidates.source_access: Open full text in PMC; Methods §§2.1-2.2, Results §3.1 and Table 1 inspected.
candidates.food_and_matrix: Allium cepa edible onion samples purchased in Sobetsu-area markets/supermarket, June/July and December 2013; planting/season/origin differ between summer and winter.
candidates.analyte_and_form: Quercetin aglycone measured after acid hydrolysis of freeze-dried foods; the result includes aglycone liberated from glycosides and is not free aglycone alone.
candidates.raw_cooked_conditions: Onion (200 g × 2) was cooked by stir-frying before lyophilization; the text separately describes sautéed onion results. Table 1 lists seasonal onion rows without a clearly paired untreated/cooked designation.
candidates.units_and_basis: mg/100 g fresh weight; edible-portion basis. The reported sentence for sautéed onion gives the same unit, but the source does not provide a usable raw/cooked matched pair with explicit cooked mass yield in the inspected tables.
candidates.yield_and_mass_balance: No cooked onion yield/retention mass balance identified in the inspected methods or tables.
candidates.analytical_method: Acid hydrolysis (90°C, 60 min), then HPLC-PDA detection at 370 nm; hydrolysis converts quercetin glycosides to aglycone before measurement.
candidates.replication: One to three market purchases per food; each sample determined in triplicate. Triplicates are analytical; the sample-level biological n is 1-3.
blockers: Hydrolyzed total quercetin aglycone equivalents differ from the directly measured free quercetin analyte in B011.
The article does not give an unambiguous paired raw-versus-sautéed onion table row and cooked yield needed for retention or cooked concentration comparison.
Season, planting type and production origin differ, and cultivar/lot matching with B011 is unavailable.

candidates.citation: Németh K, Piskula MK, Takácsová M. Effect of Boiling on Yellow Onion Quercetin (Glucosides). Czech Journal of Food Sciences. 2004;22(Special Issue):S170-S172.
candidates.source_access: Open primary publisher record and PDF; methods, figure captions and article locator inspected.
candidates.quantitative_locator: Publisher PDF, pp. S170-S172; Figure 2 is identified as transfer of dry mass and quercetin glucosides into soup under three onion:water ratios. No table of free quercetin concentration was located.
candidates.food_and_matrix: Yellow onion edible fleshy scales; inner/outer scale structure is considered.
candidates.analyte_and_form: Quercetin mono- and diglucosides (3-glucoside, 4'-glucoside, 3,4'-diglucoside); analyte focus is conjugates and redistribution into broth.
candidates.raw_cooked_conditions: Raw control, onion solids, and soup after 30 min reflux boiling at onion:water ratios 1:5, 1:10, and 1:20 by weight.
candidates.units_and_basis: Not confirmed as a fresh-weight mass concentration in the accessible article text/figure locator; solids and soup were lyophilized before extraction. Do not infer or convert a fresh-weight result.
candidates.yield_and_mass_balance: Cooking medium and onion:water ratios are specified; a quantitative cooked yield for the edible solids is not verified from the accessible locator.
candidates.analytical_method: Lyophilization, acidified methanol extraction and HPLC-UV, per the primary article abstract/method description.
candidates.replication: Not reported in the accessible paper text reviewed for this screen.
blockers: The target analytes are quercetin glycosides, not direct free quercetin aglycone.
The accessible locator does not establish compatible fresh-weight concentration units or replicate structure.
Boiling and broth transfer do not match a current Stage C cooked estimate in this workstream.

candidates.citation: Harris S, Brunton N, Tiwari U, Cummins E. Human Exposure Modelling of Quercetin in Onions (Allium cepa L.) Following Thermal Processing. Food Chemistry. 2015;187:135-139.
candidates.source_access: PubMed and publisher abstract/section preview accessible; full quantitative table content not available through inspected access.
candidates.quantitative_locator: Publisher preview identifies Table 1 as concentrations of 3,4'-Qdg and 4'-Qmg in freeze-dried fresh/control and heat-treated onion extracts; exact cells and table units were not available in accessible preview.
candidates.food_and_matrix: Local-retail Allium cepa inner flesh, Dublin, Ireland; outer layer removed.
candidates.analyte_and_form: Quercetin-3,4'-diglucoside and quercetin-4'-monoglucoside. Publisher preview states quercetin standard was run but aglycone was not detected.
candidates.raw_cooked_conditions: Frying, baking and steaming for 5, 10 and 15 min; full method details partially visible in publisher section snippets.
candidates.units_and_basis: Exact Table 1 quantitative units/basis could not be verified from accessible full text; source calls the samples freeze-dried and methanolic extracts. No fresh-weight conversion was assumed.
candidates.yield_and_mass_balance: Not verified from accessible table/method detail.
candidates.analytical_method: Chromatographic glycoside concentration analysis reported; exact calibration and full method not verified from inspected primary full text.
candidates.replication: Abstract reports onion samples n=3 and treatments by process/time; whether n denotes biological or analytical replicates was not resolved from accessible text.
blockers: Target analytes are quercetin glycosides, and the study reports no detected free quercetin aglycone.
Units, measurement basis, cooking yield and quantitative table cells could not be verified from accessible article text.
No matching Stage C prediction endpoint was available.

candidates.citation: Lombard K, Peffley E, Geoffriau E, Thompson L, Herring A. Quercetin in Onion (Allium cepa L.) after Heat-Treatment Simulating Home Preparation. Journal of Food Composition and Analysis. 2005;18(6):571-581.
candidates.source_access: Publisher article page/preview and AGRIS metadata accessible; full quantitative article table not inspected.
candidates.quantitative_locator: Publisher preview states pooled main-effect means are displayed in Table 1; tables/figures beyond the preview were not accessible for this screen.
candidates.food_and_matrix: Allium cepa bulbs from five cultivars: four yellow-skinned and one red-skinned; publisher preview describes ten randomly selected bulbs per cultivar and cold storage before cooking.
candidates.analyte_and_form: Primarily quercetin diglucoside and quercetin monoglucoside; source abstract reports the combined major conjugates and says they represent most total flavonol content. Individual free-aglycone result not verified in accessible table.
candidates.raw_cooked_conditions: Raw control and sautéing, baking, boiling; detailed cooking times/temperatures are not in the accessible quantitative preview.
candidates.units_and_basis: Not verified in accessible publisher preview; no unit or basis conversion attempted.
candidates.yield_and_mass_balance: Preview discusses water loss/concentration effects, but exact paired yield and mass data were not accessible.
candidates.analytical_method: Not sufficiently verified from accessible preview for a quantitative import.
candidates.replication: Ten bulbs per cultivar are described in preview; the article reports pooled treatment means, but treatment-level independent sample/analytical replicate details were not verified.
blockers: The article's headline measurand is dominated by glycoside forms, not directly comparable to B011's free quercetin aglycone.
Full quantitative table, calibration, units, measurement basis, cooking yields and replicate details were unavailable in inspected access.
The multi-cultivar pooled sample cannot be matched to the unspecified B011 cultivar or a Stage C cooked endpoint.

candidates.citation: Ioku K, Aoyama Y, Tokuno A, Terao J, Nakatani N, Takei Y. Various Cooking Methods and the Flavonoid Content in Onion. Journal of Nutritional Science and Vitaminology. 2001;47(1):78-83.
candidates.source_access: PubMed citation and abstract accessible; full numerical article tables not inspected.
candidates.quantitative_locator: PubMed abstract (pp. 78-83 citation); a table/figure locator was not visible in the inspected record.
candidates.food_and_matrix: Onion (Allium cepa); color, cultivar, part and sourcing are not specified in the accessible abstract.
candidates.analyte_and_form: Quercetin 4'-O-beta-glucoside and quercetin 3,4'-O-beta-diglucoside, plus total phenolics and ascorbic acid.
candidates.raw_cooked_conditions: Boiling, frying with oil or butter, and microwave cooking; exact time/temperature absent from accessible abstract.
candidates.units_and_basis: Not verified; no table data extracted.
candidates.yield_and_mass_balance: Not verified; abstract notes transfer to boiling water but no quantitative mass balance used.
candidates.analytical_method: HPLC is indexed in PubMed; full quantitative method not inspected.
blockers: Reported target is quercetin conjugates rather than direct free quercetin aglycone.
Compound-specific numeric tables, units, fresh/cooked basis, conditions and replicate details were not accessible for independent verification.
No matching Stage C cooked estimate was available.

screen_result.reason: No source provides a verified reference value that is the same direct free-quercetin measurand, in a compatible fresh-weight basis and target condition, with complete enough provenance to compare to B011-HPLC-06 or a Stage C cooked prediction without hydrolysis/calibration/matrix assumptions.
